text_devanagari: अ॒ना॒गसं॒ ब्रह्म॑णा त्वा कृणोमि शि॒वे ते॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी उ॒भे स्ता॑म् ॥ १ ॥
notes: Magnification was sufficient; line attribution was unambiguous because the page bands separate cleanly. In seg1 the anudatta bars of the line ABOVE occupy y=41-53 and those of the middle line occupy y=211-224, with fully blank rows between them and the glyph bodies (middle-line body y=103-184). In seg2 the same split is y=38-49 (line above) vs y=206-215 (middle line). Every bar I recorded lies in the lower band, i.e. under the middle line; no bar sat ambiguously between bands. Two descender shapes in that lower band are NOT accents and were excluded: the vocalic-r hook of kr in kRNomi (seg1 x1194-1236, 31px tall vs 8-11px for a true bar) and the same hook of pR in pRthivI (seg2 x625-666); the halanta tail of m in stAm (seg2 x1294-1313) was likewise excluded. Svaritas are the three thin isolated vertical strokes above the headline, 8-10px wide (seg1 x844-853 over hma of brahmaNA; seg2 x530-537 over vA of dyAvA; seg2 x1163-1170 over stA of stAm); all other components above the headline are 50-68px wide and are e/o/i/I matras. The dot at seg1 x644-663 is the anusvara of saM, not an accent. Anudattas (7): a and nA and saM of anAgasaM; shi of shive; te; thi of pRthivI; u of ubhe. Bar centres sit slightly right of aksara centre, consistently (+3 to +31px), matching the same rightward bias seen in the r-hooks. Anusvara-final saM carries its bar after the anusvara. First aksara of the line is the 1856 'a' (reads as R/shra to a modern eye). The two segments overlap by ~91px (seg1 x1523 = seg2 x46, the i-matra of shi), so no material is lost at the join. Only residual doubt is the verse numeral: a closed bowl with a straight descender and a small right foot, plus a pointed spur at upper left; read as U+0967 (1) rather than U+096F (9) on the strength of that spur. Not marked [?] since the glyph itself is sharp.
